title: used to (do)
subtitle: I used to do
summary: Use used to + verb for habits and situations that were true in the past but are not true any more.

lesson.heading: Study this situation
lesson.text: Nicola doesn't travel much these days. She prefers to stay at home. But **she used to travel** a lot. **She used to go** away two or three times a year. *She used to travel a lot* = she travelled often in the past, but she doesn't do this any more.

examples.text: A few years ago: **she used to travel**. These days: she doesn't travel.

lesson.heading: I used to do something
lesson.text: **I used to do something** = I did it often in the past, but not any more. We also use **used to ...** for things that were true, but are not true any more.

examples.text: I **used to play** tennis a lot, but I don't play very much now.
David **used to spend** a lot of money on clothes. These days he can't afford it.
'Do you go to the cinema much?' 'Not now, but **I used to**.' (= I used to go)
This building is now a furniture shop. It **used to be** a cinema.
I've started drinking coffee recently. I **never used to like** it before.
Lisa **used to have** very long hair when she was a child.

lesson.heading: used to is past - there is no present
lesson.note: You cannot say 'I use to do'. To talk about the present, use the present simple: We used to live in a small village, but now we live in a city. There used to be four cinemas in the town. Now there is only one.

lesson.heading: Questions and negatives
lesson.text: The normal question form is **did (you) use to ... ?** The negative form is **didn't use to ...** (used not to ... is also possible).

examples.text: **Did you use to eat** a lot of sweets when you were a child? (= did you do this often?)
I **didn't use to like** him. (or I used not to like him.)

lesson.heading: I used to do or I was doing?

left.label: I used to do
left.text: A past habit that has stopped.
examples: I **used to watch** TV a lot. (= I watched TV often in the past, but I don't do this any more)

right.label: I was doing
right.text: In the middle of an action at a past moment.
examples: I **was watching** TV when Rob called. (= I was in the middle of watching TV)

lesson.heading: I used to do or I am used to doing?

left.label: I used to do
examples: I **used to live** alone. (= I lived alone in the past, but I no longer live alone.)

right.label: I am used to doing
right.text: Present, and it is not a problem for me.
examples: I **am used to living** alone. (= I live alone, and it's not a problem for me because I've lived alone for some time.)

lesson.note: The structures and the meanings are different - do not confuse them.

lesson.text: Spelling check: after did or didn't the form is use to (Did you use to ... ? / I didn't use to ...), everywhere else it is used to.

exercises.prompt: Nicola doesn't travel much these days, but she ___ a lot.
exercises.explanation: A past habit that has stopped: used to + verb. There is no present form.

exercises.prompt: Sophie ___ a motorbike, but last year she sold it and bought a car.
exercises.explanation: She had (or rode) a motorbike in the past but not now: used to have / used to ride.

exercises.prompt: Our friends moved to Spain a few years ago. They ___ in Paris.
exercises.explanation: A past situation that is no longer true: They used to live in Paris.

exercises.prompt: Karen has changed a lot in ten years. Match how she used to be with how she is today.

pairs.left: She used to travel a lot,
pairs.right: but she doesn't go away much these days.

pairs.left: She used to be very lazy,
pairs.right: but she works very hard these days.

pairs.left: She didn't use to like cheese,
pairs.right: but she eats lots of it now.

pairs.left: She used to play the piano,
pairs.right: but she hasn't played for a long time.

pairs.left: She didn't use to drink tea,
She used to have a dog,
pairs.right: but it died two years ago.

exercises.prompt: Jackie ___ my best friend, but we aren't friends any more.
exercises.explanation: Something that was true in the past but not now: used to be.

exercises.prompt: Make a question about someone's childhood habits.
exercises.answer: Did you use to eat a lot of sweets when you were a child?
exercises.explanation: The question form is did + subject + use to + verb.

exercises.statement: I use to play tennis a lot, but I don't play very much now.
exercises.explanation: I used to play tennis a lot. Used to is past; the form 'I use to' does not exist.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I was in the middle of watching TV'?
options: I was watching TV when Rob called.
I used to watch TV a lot.
I am used to watching TV.
exercises.explanation: Was doing = in the middle of an action at a past moment. Used to = a past habit that has stopped.

exercises.prompt: There ___ a hotel near the airport, but it closed a long time ago.
exercises.explanation: There used to be = there was in the past, but not now.

exercises.statement: There used to be four cinemas in the town. Now there is only one.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Used to be describes a past situation; the present simple (there is) describes now.

exercises.prompt: These days I eat more than before. I ___ use to eat as much.
exercises.explanation: The negative form is didn't use to (used not to is also possible).

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I live alone now, and it's not a problem for me'?
options: I am used to living alone.
exercises.explanation: I am used to doing = I am accustomed to it now. I used to do = I did it in the past but not any more.
